rules.title: Permitted no-fault eviction reasons under RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance may end a tenancy for a no-fault reason only on listed grounds: occupancy by the owner, close family or a required resident manager; demolition, conversion or removal from rental use (Ellis Act); a government order to vacate; HUD sale; or conversion to affordable housing. Each requires relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Listed no-fault grounds only; relocation required
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
rules.exemptions: Evictions for resident manager occupancy are allowed only if required by law, an affordable housing covenant, or a regulatory agreement.

rules.title: Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict and filing of termination notice with LAHD
rules.requirement: Before a no-fault eviction from an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD. The termination notice may be served only after that filing, and a copy must be filed with LAHD within 3 days of service.
rules.key_value: Notice copy filed with LAHD within 3 days of service
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault evictions from RSO or JCO units in Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord files the Declaration with LAHD, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO; the tenant may raise this as a defense.

rules.title: Relocation assistance amounts for no-fault evictions (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027)
rules.requirement: For a no-fault eviction from an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must pay relocation assistance per unit. Eligible tenants get $11,000 (less than 3 years' tenancy) or $14,400 (3 or more years, or low income). Qualified tenants (age 62+, disabled, or with minor children) get $23,150 or $27,400.
rules.key_value: Eligible $11,000/$14,400; Qualified $23,150/$27,400; Mom & Pop $10,550/$21,250; JCO single-family owned by natural person: one month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault evictions from RSO or JCO units. The amounts rise every July 1.
rules.exemptions: Mom and Pop properties pay a reduced amount for owner or relative occupancy evictions. A JCO single-family home owned by a natural person owes one month's rent. No payment is due when replacing a resident manager or for natural-disaster hazards not caused by the landlord. Accumulated unpaid rent may be offset except for government orders to vacate.
rules.penalty: The tenant may raise non-payment as an affirmative defense to eviction, file a complaint with LAHD, or bring a private right of action.

exemption_tests.description: Mom and Pop reduced relocation ($10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified) for owner or relative occupancy evictions only: the building has 4 or fewer units, the provision was not used in the prior 3 years, the landlord owns no more than 4 units plus one single-family home in the City, and the relative owns no LA residential property.
JCO single-family dwelling owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home in the City: relocation is one month's rent.

rules.title: Timing and method of relocation payment
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance must be made available within 15 days of serving the eviction notice and split equally among co-tenants. A landlord may instead fund an escrow account within those 15 days that pays the tenant's moving costs within 3 working days of a request.
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault evictions from RSO or JCO units.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units
rules.requirement: If a Protected Unit (including every RSO unit) is demolished for new construction, lower-income tenants (80% AMI or below) must get enhanced relocation. Under the standardized option this is $115,480 (extremely low), $96,750 (very low) or $87,450 (low income). Tenants above low income get the RSO/JCO amounts, and the owner pays whichever amount is highest.
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict.
rules.exemptions: Units that are not Protected Units or not occupied by lower-income tenants get the regular RSO/JCO amounts.

rules.title: RPO occupant protections: right to remain, return and first refusal
rules.requirement: Tenants of Protected Units being demolished for new construction may stay until 6 months before construction starts and must get a 6-month notice to move out. They may return if the demolition does not proceed, and some have a right of first refusal in the new building.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income households displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced when their units are demolished for new construction must get relocation benefits equal to those public entities pay under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq. In Los Angeles, the owner pays the HCA amount or the city amount, whichever is higher.

rules.coverage_conditions: Protected units demolished for new housing development; lower-income occupants.

notes: The document is an LAHD bulletin, so the state Housing Crisis Act rule is a secondary restatement. Bulletin B has inconsistent dates: its fee chart is headed 'Effective July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026', but the same fee amounts appear in Bulletin A as July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The LAHD administrative fees paid by landlords are not tenant application or screening fees, so they were not extracted. The RSO coverage cutoff (built on or before Oct 1978) is not stated in this document, so the coverage fields are left null. The Mom & Pop and single-family relocation amounts are recorded as exemption tests on the main relocation rule. Some quoted_spans end with a trailing space so they match the source exactly.
